name: EPSS (Exploit Prediction Scoring System), FIRST
owner: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST)
gives: a daily probability, per published CVE, that it will be exploited in the next 30 days (cve, epss, percentile)

why.quote: EPSS scores are published daily, free of charge, with no registration required. [...] Attribution is requested when EPSS data is used in publications or products.
why.basis: EPSS data page and FAQ. No licence is named for the scores. FIRST Services Terms of Use (https://www.first.org/about/policies/terms, v1.0.0, September 2023) allow viewing, copying and distributing content for vulnerability disclosure, incident response or preventative cybersecurity uses, and other uses need FIRST written permission; EPSS is not named there, so whether they apply is unclear.

licence.name: unclear (no licence named; FIRST Services Terms may apply)

interface: Daily full file https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-current.csv.gz (redirects; cve, epss, percentile); archive github.com/empiricalsec/epss_scores back to 2021-04-14. API https://api.first.org/data/v1/epss is for lookups, not bulk (1000 requests a minute unauthenticated). robots.txt at www.first.org disallows only /signin and /_/links; api.first.org has none (404).
notes: Asked by cyber.b@ (19 Nov 2026 about 01:24 UTC) for the every-prediction-is-kept-and-checked guidance: keep each day's scores as read, check after 30 days against CISA KEV additions, worldwide totals only. EPSS is itself a prediction, so it fits. Not read until Dinis (or rights@) decides whether FIRST's terms allow a free public data site, and whether commercial use stays off.
how: Not collected. Waiting on Dinis: do FIRST's Services Terms cover EPSS, and is our use (a free public site showing daily totals and a track record, for preventative cybersecurity) within them?
